options.text: Take each prime at its highest power: $2^{2}\times 3\times 7=84$.
Take only the primes that appear in both factorisations: $2\times 7=14$.
Multiply every printed prime power from both lists without trimming: $2^{2}\times 7\times 2\times 3\times 7$.
The LCM is $28$, because $28$ is the first number printed.

teacher.key_rationale: LCM needs each prime at its highest power across the factorisations: 2²×3×7=84. Using only shared primes is HCF, not LCM. Keeping duplicate primes overcounts. Picking the first printed number is surface capture.

stem:
Sagar has $28=2^{2}\times 7$ and $42=2\times 3\times 7$. He wants their LCM from these prime factorisations.

Which plan is correct?
